explanation: Simulate an inorder traversal of a balanced tree: recursively build half the nodes, consume the next original list node as root, then build the remaining nodes. Advance the list cursor before overwriting its next link.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Every node is consumed once, with constant local link work.
spaceComplexity: O(log n) recursion space; original nodes are reused. Balanced half-size recursion has logarithmic depth; nodes are reused.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: Build(size) consumes exactly size consecutive original list nodes and returns them in the same inorder order. Inductively, its left call consumes the first size / 2 nodes, the next node becomes root, and the right call consumes the remainder. Sorted list order therefore makes every left value at most the root and every right value at least it. The chosen subtree sizes differ by at most one.
walkthrough: For sorted list [-6, -1, 5, 12, 19], build the first two nodes as the left subtree, consume 5 as root, and build the remaining two nodes as the right subtree. The resulting tree has root 5, left root -1 with left child -6, and right root 19 with left child 12. Its inorder contents remain [-6, -1, 5, 12, 19]; the adapter verdict is true.
edgeCases: count = 0 returns null without consuming a node.
A single list node becomes a leaf.
The next-list cursor advances before Right is overwritten as a tree-child link; duplicate contents remain present in inorder.
